story: On a hazy Saturday afternoon in Sumter Oaks, Gary is pulling cold drinks and a bag of ice from his fridge to take over to Rosa's tonight, while Donna studies the ladder standings at the Rec Center to see how far her team has to climb. Out on Magnolia Loop, Hal and Rosa are sorting out the evening: he promises his cornbread and folding table will arrive early, and she asks him to help with the chairs around five before doors open at six. Everyone seems content in the warm 85-degree heat, with Donna determined and Rosa looking forward to the night ahead.
events: Gary (gary fridge): Pull out the cold drinks and a bag of ice to bring to Rosa's tonight
Donna (ladder standings board): Study the ladder standings to see who our next opponents are and how far we need to climb

gary.thought_process: It's a little after four on Saturday. The review application is filed and still pending, so the cart stays in the garage, nothing mounted outside. I've already staged the hardware, bench-tested the speaker and light strip, and pre-routed the wiring under the seat. Saturday at five I'm due at Rosa's with Donna, and I'm not showing up empty-handed. The cobbler and ice are covered, but the cooler is mine to bring. Grabbing something from the fridge for the table is a useful way to spend the hour, and it keeps me from fidgeting with the cart and breaking my own rule. Then I head over to Magnolia Loop.

parameters.content: Pull out the cold drinks and a bag of ice to bring to Rosa's tonight

donna.thought_process: I've reserved the court and drilled third-shot drops against the cones, and it's 4:17 PM with Gary still not here. Nobody is in line-of-sight, so there's no one to talk to. I booked the slot and told Gary the time, so he should turn up soon. I'll check the ladder standings board to see who we're up against, then he'll hopefully show and we can get in real practice before Rosa's Saturday dinner. Keeps me productive instead of pacing.

parameters.content: Study the ladder standings to see who our next opponents are and how far we need to climb

hal.thought_process: I'm on Magnolia Loop with the cornbread and table plan in mind, and Rosa is right here in line-of-sight. Saturday dinner is at her place, and showing up on time without a fuss is the point. A short, civil word about heading her way fits what I want: order, respect, and keeping my word. My old notices are cleared and the flamingos are behind the hedge, so there's no reason to stir up anything else. I'll let her know I'm coming and ask whether she wants the table in early.

parameters.content: Afternoon, Rosa. I've got the cornbread and the folding table ready, so I'll be at your door early. Tell me where you want the table and I'll carry it in without any fuss.

rosa.thought_process: Hal just walked up on Magnolia Loop, and it's 4:17 PM with the dinner tonight. His cornbread is the one thing I haven't seen yet, and I still need to finish dinner prep, so a short, friendly check-in is the right move. I won't repeat any earlier invitation, just confirm timing and keep it moving.

parameters.content: Hal, good timing. Is that cornbread on track for tonight? Doors open at six, and I could use an extra hand with the chairs if you're free around five.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
